name: Qhapaq Ñan, Andean Road System
countries: Peru, Chile, Ecuador, Colombia, Argentina, Bolivia (Plurinational State of)
description: The Qhapaq Ñan is the Inca "royal road," a web of paths that ran through six South American countries, from glaciated Andean passes above 6,000 metres down to the coast, rainforest and desert. The Incas built it without wheels, using stairways, bridges and retaining walls, and lined it with relay stations, storehouses and fortresses. Today 273 sites along more than 6,000 km are protected, and the Inca Trail to Machu Picchu is its best-known stretch.
